nodes.name: launch.ts
nodes.summary: Wraps Process.spawn for LSP server processes, forcing piped stdin/stdout/stderr and asserting all three streams are available before returning the child.

nodes.name: spawn
nodes.summary: Spawns an LSP server process with piped stdio, accepting either (cmd, args, opts) or (cmd, opts) overload signatures.

nodes.name: lsp.ts
nodes.summary: Effect service (@opencode/LSP) managing LSP client lifecycle: matches servers to files by extension, spawns clients per workspace root with in-flight dedupe and exponential backoff for broken servers, and exposes hover/definition/references/symbols/call-hierarchy queries across all matching clients.
nodes.languageNotes: Effect Context.Service + Layer.effect pattern; per-project state kept in InstanceState; broken-server backoff is exponential (max 30s) with a 5-minute TTL reset.

nodes.name: layer
nodes.summary: Effect layer building the LSP service: merges built-in and config-defined servers, spawns clients per file/root with in-flight dedupe and exponential backoff for failing servers, and proxies LSP requests (hover, definition, references, symbols, call hierarchy) to all matching clients.

nodes.name: server.ts
nodes.summary: Registry of 38 language server definitions (TypeScript, Go, Rust, C#, Java, Kotlin, Python, and more), each declaring file extensions, workspace-root detection, and spawn logic — including auto-download and installation of missing servers into the global bin directory.
nodes.languageNotes: Each server is an exported `Info` const object with a root-finding function and an async spawn(); NearestRoot is a shared factory that walks up the directory tree looking for lockfile markers.

nodes.name: NearestRoot
nodes.summary: Root-finder factory that walks up from a file toward the instance directory looking for marker files such as lockfiles, with optional exclusion patterns that suppress root detection entirely.

nodes.name: venv.ts
nodes.summary: Resolves the Python interpreter path from $VIRTUAL_ENV or common .venv/venv directories under the project root, used by the Python LSP servers (Pyright, Ty).

nodes.name: venvCandidates
nodes.summary: Lists candidate virtualenv directories: $VIRTUAL_ENV, .venv, and venv under the given root.

nodes.name: resolveVenvPython
nodes.summary: Returns the first existing Python binary across venv candidates, handling the Windows Scripts/python.exe layout versus bin/python on Unix.

nodes.name: markdown.d.ts
nodes.summary: Ambient TypeScript declaration allowing .md files to be imported as string content modules.

nodes.name: AGENTS.md
nodes.summary: Developer notes on MCP internals: tool permission keys use the mcp_ prefix, permission patterns derive from tool args rather than always ["*"], and MCP tools are filtered through Permission.disabled().

nodes.name: auth.ts
nodes.summary: Effect service (@opencode/McpAuth) persisting MCP OAuth tokens, client info, code verifiers, and OAuth state to mcp-auth.json with 0600 permissions, providing field-level update helpers and token expiry checks.

nodes.name: layer
nodes.summary: Effect layer implementing the McpAuth service over mcp-auth.json; generic updateField/clearField factories generate the per-field token, client-info, verifier, and state operations.

nodes.name: index.ts
nodes.summary: The MCP client manager (@opencode/MCP): connects local stdio and remote HTTP/SSE servers with OAuth orchestration, converts MCP tools into AI SDK dynamic tools, and exposes prompts/resources with per-server status tracking and bus events.
nodes.languageNotes: Bridges the MCP SDK's own zod version with the workspace zod via tolerant loose-object schemas and boundary casts; remote servers try StreamableHTTP transport first, then SSE fallback.

nodes.name: listTools
nodes.summary: Lists tools from an MCP client with a tolerant retry path that bypasses output-schema validation errors via a raw tools/list request.

nodes.name: convertMcpTool
nodes.summary: Converts an MCP tool definition into an AI SDK dynamicTool with a normalized JSON schema object and a callTool executor using timeout with progress-based reset.

nodes.name: fetchFromClient
nodes.summary: Generic wrapper that lists named items (prompts/resources) from an MCP client and indexes them under sanitized client:name keys, swallowing per-client errors.

nodes.name: layer
nodes.summary: Effect layer for the MCP service: stdio/remote transport creation with StreamableHTTP-then-SSE fallback, OAuth flows via McpOAuthProvider and the local callback server, cached tools/prompts/resources per server, and status-change bus events with TUI toasts for auth requirements.

nodes.name: oauth-callback.ts
nodes.summary: Local HTTP callback server (default port 19876) that receives OAuth redirect codes for MCP authorization, correlating pending flows by state with a 5-minute timeout and browser-friendly success/error pages.

nodes.name: handleRequest
nodes.summary: Handles the OAuth redirect request: validates state against pending auths, resolves or rejects the waiting flow, and renders styled HTML success/error pages.

nodes.name: ensureRunning
nodes.summary: Starts the single shared callback HTTP server if not already listening, rebinding port and path from a custom redirect URI.

nodes.name: waitForCallback
nodes.summary: Registers a pending auth by oauthState and resolves with the authorization code when the redirect arrives, timing out after 5 minutes.

nodes.name: oauth-provider.ts
nodes.summary: Implements the MCP SDK's OAuthClientProvider interface backed by the McpAuth store: supplies client metadata, authorization redirects, token persistence, and PKCE state for remote MCP server authorization.

nodes.name: McpOAuthProvider
nodes.summary: OAuthClientProvider implementation storing tokens, client information, code verifiers, and state through McpAuth; publishes authorization redirects via callback and invalidates stored credentials on auth failure.

nodes.name: parseRedirectUri
nodes.summary: Extracts port and path from a redirect URI for configuring the callback server.

nodes.name: node.ts
nodes.summary: Barrel re-exporting Node-only entry points (Config, Server, bootstrap, Database, JsonMigration) for consumers that run the full server runtime.

nodes.name: index.ts
nodes.summary: Parses the apply_patch format (Add/Update/Delete File with @@ hunks) and computes new file contents from matched chunks using exact, fuzzy, ambiguity-aware, and backward context search with BOM handling.
nodes.languageNotes: Pure parsing/derivation layer with no filesystem IO — the caller reads original files and writes results; matcher comparators come from tool/matcher.

nodes.name: parsePatchHeader
nodes.summary: Parses *** Add/Delete/Update File headers including Move to and Force Move to directives, returning the file path, move target, force flag, and next line index.

nodes.name: parseUpdateFileChunks
nodes.summary: Parses @@ context-headed hunks with keep/remove/add change lines, rejecting malformed lines and empty hunks while tracking End of File markers.

nodes.name: parseAddFileContent
nodes.summary: Collects the raw content lines of an Add File block until the next *** directive, stripping heredoc fences.

nodes.name: parsePatch
nodes.summary: Top-level parser turning apply_patch text into Hunk[] operations (add, delete, update with optional move) by delegating to the header and chunk parsers.

nodes.name: deriveNewContentsFromChunks
nodes.summary: Applies parsed update chunks to the original file content, producing the new full file text via replacement computation.

nodes.name: computeReplacements
nodes.summary: Locates each chunk's old_lines within the original file using exact, fuzzy, ambiguity-aware, and backward pattern search, resolving the line ranges to replace.

nodes.name: applyReplacements
nodes.summary: Splices computed replacements into the line array in descending order so earlier offsets stay valid.

nodes.name: seekSequence
nodes.summary: Finds a line sequence in the file supporting EOF anchoring, uniqueness requirements, and forward/backward search with comparator-based matching.

nodes.name: AGENTS.md
nodes.summary: Developer notes on the permission engine: disabled() only hides tools on catch-all deny, Wildcard.match is exact glob matching, evaluate() is last-match-wins defaulting to ask, ask() ordering between DB-persisted approvals and config rules, plus known flaky-test caveats.
